reason: The text passage (Exodus 2:1-10) describes the birth and early childhood of Moses as an infant. The narrative focuses on his rescue from the Nile River and his upbringing first by his mother and then by Pharaoh's daughter. Moses is depicted as a passive subject—being hidden, placed in a basket, found, and raised—with no portrayal of him as a national leader or harboring any leadership aspirations. At this narrative stage, he is merely a child, not yet capable of or characterized as having any political or national leadership role.
